title: ChatGPT Joins BCCI as Associate Partner in ₹130-Crore Home Cricket Deal
excerpt: OpenAI's AI assistant will share associate partner rights with Campa Cola and SBI Life across 35 bilateral matches through March 2028, marking AI's first major cricket sponsorship.
body:
• The BCCI has named ChatGPT, Campa Cola, and SBI Life as Associate Partners for India's home cricket season through March 2028, covering 35 bilateral matches.
  • The combined deal is valued at over ₹130 crore, representing a 44% increase over the previous partnership cycle.
  • ChatGPT and SBI Life will each pay ₹1.2 crore per match, while Campa Cola bid the highest at ₹1.31 crore per match.
  • The deal marks the first time an AI company has entered Indian cricket sponsorship, reflecting the technology sector's growing appetite for sports marketing.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has entered Indian cricket as the BCCI announced the AI-powered assistant as one of three new Associate Partners for India's home season. The partnership, unveiled on Monday, pairs ChatGPT with Reliance-owned Campa Cola and SBI Life Insurance across 35 bilateral matches through March 2028.

The three deals carry a combined value of over ₹130 crore — approximately ₹129.85 crore across all matches — representing a 44 per cent increase over the previous associate partnership cycle. The arrangement begins with India's upcoming home series against the West Indies.

Breaking Down the Numbers

Campa Cola, owned by Reliance Consumer Products, emerged as the highest bidder at ₹1.31 crore per match. ChatGPT and SBI Life each bid ₹1.2 crore per match, bringing the combined per-match value to approximately ₹3.71 crore. Bisleri and Indian Oil Corporation also reportedly quoted ₹1.2 crore per match but did not secure the final positions.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2097333641810780368

"A 44% increase in the combined deal value, with the latest partnerships valued at over ₹130 crore, is a significant achievement and demonstrates the strong demand for association with Indian cricket."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Honorary Secretary

BCCI President Mithun Manhas described the signings as "a strong endorsement of the strength of the Indian cricket ecosystem," adding that the increased deal value reflects the trust that major brands place in Indian cricket's commercial potential.

AI Enters Cricket Sponsorship

ChatGPT's inclusion marks a notable milestone — the first time an artificial intelligence company has become part of the BCCI's commercial portfolio. The move extends OpenAI's marketing push beyond its core technology audience into mainstream Indian entertainment, leveraging cricket's unmatched reach across the country.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=JwOLaEuES-g

India's home cricket season draws hundreds of millions of viewers across television and digital platforms, making it one of the most valuable sports properties in the world. For OpenAI, the association offers exposure to a massive consumer base at a time when ChatGPT is competing with Google's Gemini and other AI assistants for dominance in the Indian market.

A Diverse Commercial Mix

The three partners span distinctly different industries. Campa Cola represents the revival of an iconic Indian beverage brand under Reliance's ownership, bringing nostalgia and mass-market consumer appeal. SBI Life, India's leading life insurance provider, extends its existing sports marketing strategy. Together with ChatGPT, the trio reflects how cricket sponsorship is broadening beyond traditional categories like consumer goods and automobiles.

The BCCI noted that the diversity of partners highlights the range of commercial opportunities available through India's home season. Saikia said the three brands "represent three very different and exciting categories" and that the board looks forward to creating "new ways to engage with fans and enhance their experience."

Title Sponsorship Still Open

The associate partner deals come as the BCCI continues its search for a new title sponsor for India's home international matches. The previous title sponsorship agreement ended in August 2026, and the board had invited bids for both tiers earlier this year. By locking in the associate deals first, the BCCI has secured significant commercial commitments while the higher-profile title sponsorship negotiations continue.

With 35 matches spread across two seasons, the partnerships will give all three brands sustained visibility through India's packed bilateral calendar — a schedule that includes series against the West Indies, England, Australia, and other top sides over the next 18 months.
